correctness.rationale: Independently built the LCF graph and reproduced girth seven. Enumerated disjoint edge subsets in the two halves of the edge list and joined them by complementary covered-vertex sets; this gives each perfect matching once. Evaluated Walsh signs by parity sums using a different spanning tree from the frozen verifier, and inverted the range indicator by separable direct summation. All nine histogram entries, 60 matchings, 2112 reduced zeros, full rank 51,002,736,640 and nullity 17,716,740,096 agree. The connected cut space has dimension 23, and tree restriction on it is bijective by propagation along the tree; signs differ only by a common global factor within each coset, so the histogram lifts by 2^23. Direct original-edge character evaluation gives no singleton zeros, exactly 128 pair zeros, all disjoint, and edge incidences 20 throughout. Fourier inversion gives zero off the cycle space, with exactly 2412 nonzero coordinates inside and absolute integer coefficient sum 120192 on the 8192-point quotient, hence endpoint norm 939/64. A convolution has this same kernel absolute sum as either the maximum column sum or maximum row sum. Translating and averaging any projection onto the invariant range keeps its range and its identity action there, contracts the norm, and forces the unique convolution projection. Thus the norm is sharp for all real or complex projections at both endpoints.
residual_risks: The 2412 support is the projection kernel's support, not the nullity. Only the specified graph and unnormalized matching convolution were checked.

value.rationale: The (3,7)-cage is a canonical extremal graph. The exact parity cancellations and endpoint range-projection amplification are meaningful Fourier recovery benchmarks on its matching incidence cube. The 2412-support fact and optimal norm use the zero locus, not the previously published total of 60, its cycle types, or merely its graph symmetries. The graph-specific exact results, not the general algorithm, warrant the value assessment.
residual_risks: No optimal inverse on other data spaces, general new projection formalism, or all-cage pattern is claimed.
